properties.name: A design takes a chunk of another design in one call: each node copied with provenance imported from the source, linked back to its origin, proposed until the taker's owner accepts, and watched so the taker learns when an origin moves
properties.statement:
A tool (take_from_design, or receive_from_design widened to a chunk) takes a chunk of a source design the caller may read: a topic neighbourhood (as topic_report gathers it) or a region from a seed and depth (as claim_region computes it), shown to the caller before anything is written. It writes each node into the taker with provenance imported, source naming the far design, an xref reference back to each origin, and ids renamed or namespaced so none collides with the taker's own; every copied requirement or decision is proposed until the taker's owner accepts it, as receive_from_design does for one. The taker owns the copies and may reword them. upstream_status reports when an origin has moved since the chunk was taken, so the taker can look; it never pulls the change in. On flo2.io the host does the read and the write for hosted designs; locally the person's reflow2 does.
Anthony, 2026-10-10: "add oauth key:values from flo2 to storyflow. Then storyflow doesn't have to retrieve how to do oauth properly, it can just inherit from flo2's implementation ... having one design just take 'chunks' of another design would be cool." He kept option (a) of dec:idea-a-design-takes-a-chunk-of-another-design-and-inherits-it over reference-only (b) and live inheritance (c). Kept beside it: a copy is a fork, and this makes the drift visible rather than preventing it; the chunk's boundary is a judgement, so the call shows it first; the origin's authorship stays visible through the xref while the copy is credited to the taker as imported.
